verdicts.title: docs/limitations.md, the page the user guide links as the safety page, contains no privacy-correctness limitation at all while high-severity ones are tracked open and other pages assert the opposite
verdicts.reasoning: The inventory is factually right: I read docs/limitations.md end to end (9 sections: MF workloads, PRNG threat model, telemetry, gradient checkpointing, FA2, DDP-only, kernel patching, vmap in-place, vmap control flow) and none is a privacy-correctness caveat; docs/user-guide/index.md:81 and mkdocs.yml:116 do link it as the reference/safety page. But that is not an independent defect. Every item the finding wants added is the user-visible shadow of a mechanism bug tracked elsewhere: BandMF participation sensitivity is open #359 (body: 'BandMfStrategy.sensitivity() is normalized to 1 for every participation context'), BLT min-sep precondition is open #595, the bounded-Gaussian mismatch is open #344, and the mf_band+poisson pairing is finding 103 in this same batch. The page states nothing false; a Known-Limitations page documents design constraints, not the open bug tracker, and each 'missing' entry evaporates the moment its underlying issue is fixed. The two genuinely wrong sentences the finding leans on (docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:96 'same accounting'; docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:142 blessing mf_band+poisson) are on other pages and belong to the findings that own those defects (dp-sgd.md:96 to #344, training-arguments.md:142 to finding 103). Filing this separately would send an engineer to rewrite prose that the real fixes will rewrite anyway.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No independent failure. docs/limitations.md accurately describes the functional/compatibility limitations it covers and makes no false privacy claim. The reader harm the finding describes is produced by (a) the open mechanism bugs #359 / #595 / #344, (b) the mf_band+poisson pairing reported as finding 103, and (c) the false 'same accounting' sentence at docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:96 — each of which is tracked or reported in its own right. Adding warnings to limitations.md is one possible remediation of those items, not a defect of this page.

verdicts.title: DPTrainer blesses mf_band + sampling_mode="poisson", which pairs the BandMF cyclic-Poisson accountant with a plain full-dataset PoissonSampler
verdicts.reasoning: Every link reproduced on the current tree. (1) _training_arguments.py:185-193 really does allow mf_band -> {'b_min_sep','poisson'} with the comment 'looser-but-valid alternative' at :182-184; validation at :1048 accepts it; tests/opaque_transformers/test_config.py:550 test_mf_band_accepts_poisson_override pins it; docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:142 documents it. (2) _dpftrl.py:224-233 dispatches sampling_mode=='poisson' to opaque.dpsgd.sampling.PoissonSampler over the whole dataset with no bands argument, while the module's own CyclicPoissonSampler branch (:281-293) is unreachable from config (cyclic_poisson is not in _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS for any mechanism). (3) _dpftrl.py:126-152 builds _ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy)) = CyclicPoisson, whose pld_at (_poisson.py:178-201) composes only num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands) per-group Poisson-Gaussian PLDs at rate sample_rate with effective_nm = nm / sensitivity, and BandMfStrategy.sensitivity (_band_mf.py:128-130) returns ||coefs|| = 1.0 ignoring min_sep/max_participations. Measured: build_amplifier_factory(poisson, band_mf_strategy(bands=10), q=256/50000, n_steps=1000)(1.0) -> CyclicPoisson, epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.35499, sensitivity 1.0. The CyclicPoisson analysis is exactly Algorithm 2 / Theorem 4 of arXiv:2306.08153 (cyclic partition; a record has exactly one eligible round per band-block), and CyclicPoissonSampler implements that (docstring/_sample_step: group_idx = step % bands, Bernoulli(sample_rate) inside the active group). Plain Poisson violates it two ways I quantified: per band-block of 10 rounds the record is eligible 10 times, so its per-group participation probability is 1-(1-q)^10 = 0.0500 rather than the charged q = 0.00512 (composing the same 100 groups at the realistic 0.0500 gives eps 3.505 vs the reported 0.355, ~10x); and multiple participations inside one block have overlapping band supports, so the true min-sep-1 sensitivity of the same 10-banded C is 1.921 at k=2, 7.967 at k=10, 11.82 at k=18 (_native.toeplitz_minsep_sensitivity_squared) against the charged 1.0. No runtime warning is emitted anywhere on this path; _dpftrl.py:217-220 asserts the opposite ('the runtime sampler cannot desync from the accountant'). Not a duplicate: #320 and its sub-issue #356 (the sampler-accounting contract) were both CLOSED as completed on 2026-08-27 and this pairing still ships and is test-pinned; open #359 covers only the sensitivity semantics of BandMfStrategy, not the sampler/amplifier pairing, and the fix here is independent (drop 'poisson' from mf_band's allow-list, or route it to CyclicPoissonSampler).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainingArguments(privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band', sampling_mode='poisson', privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bands': 10}) on a 50k-row dataset, batch 256, 1000 steps passes validation and trains with opaque.dpsgd.sampling.PoissonSampler over the full dataset every step, while the accountant is CyclicPoisson: 100 per-group Poisson-Gaussian PLDs at rate q=0.00512 and sensitivity 1.0, reporting epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.355. The deployed sampler gives each record ~10 eligible rounds per band-block (per-group participation probability 0.0500, ~b*q) and permits participations at separation 1, whose true sensitivity for the same banded C reaches 7.97 at 10 participations. Recomputing only the per-group inclusion probability at its realistic 0.0500 already yields 3.505, so the published epsilon understates the cost of the configuration the trainer blesses by roughly an order of magnitude, with no warning and a test (test_mf_band_accepts_poisson_override) pinning the pairing as intended.

verdicts.title: mu-GDP one-run audit substitutes v_k = 0.5 for every rank past 2000 and calls it "conservative" — it is the anti-conservative direction under Xiang et al. Theorem 3
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly. _gdp.py:329-334 caps exact ranks at _MAX_EXACT_RANKS=2000 and hands n_trunc = r - r' ranks to _chernoff_lower_tail as Bernoulli(0.5); _compute_v_k:368 clips v_k into [0, 0.5], so 0.5 is an upper bound on every true v_k, and Pr[sum V_k <= u] is decreasing in the v_k — the substituted value therefore makes the computed p-value smaller than the Theorem-3 bound it is supposed to over-estimate, so it is not a valid p-value. Measured with the shipped functions (n=20000, r=8000, mu=1.0, u=1396): truncated p-value 0.0 vs exact 0.0909 — rejects where the valid bound does not. The comment's rationale is also measurably false: sum of the exact top-2000 v_k = 193.34 while the substituted block contributes 3000.0 and the true sum over all 8000 ranks is 1470.4, so the truncated block dominates rather than the kept one. End to end, _best_r_u always returns r = m (_estimate.py:147-161), so any audit with more than 2000 canaries truncates; replaying _mu_at with and without the cap at significance 0.05 gives m=r=3000, u=900 -> 1.0538 shipped vs 0.9277 exact, and n=20000, r=4000, u=1100 -> 1.0689 vs 0.4919. Severity dropped from high to medium: the sole direction of the error is an inflated audited mu-hat / epsilon lower bound, i.e. the audit over-states leakage (false alarm on a correct implementation, or the RuntimeError path at :80-89); it can never hide a real privacy loss. Duplicate: open #376 'Calibrate one-run auditing under the null' names this defect in its body ('truncated-rank bounds are not calibrated for large audits') and its acceptance criteria ('Large-m truncation is exercised and conservative relative to a higher exact-rank limit'), so this is tracked, not new.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any one-run audit with more than 2000 canaries (r = m always) prices the remaining r-2000 ranks at v_k = 0.5, an upper bound on each true v_k, which lowers the Chernoff p-value below the Theorem-3 bound it must upper-bound. Measured: n=20000, r=8000, mu=1.0, u=1396 gives p = 0.0 shipped vs 0.0909 exact (rejects vs does not reject at alpha=0.05); m=r=3000, u=900 reports mu-hat 1.054 instead of 0.928. The audit therefore reports an inflated privacy-loss lower bound (or raises RuntimeError when the p-value never rises to significance), producing false 'implementation leaks more than the theory allows' alarms; it never under-reports leakage.

verdicts.title: Truncated-Poisson accounting cites the unresolvable key [Gan25] and does not document the dataset-size-dependent adjacency its guarantee assumes
verdicts.reasoning: Citation half verified: repository-wide search finds exactly three occurrences of 'Gan25' (truncated_poisson.rs:20, :125 and opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_cross_validation.py:369), no bibliography entry anywhere, and no occurrence of arXiv 2508.15089 or of a Ganesh truncated-Poisson reference in any source, doc, or Cargo/pyproject metadata — the only 'Ganesh' hits are the unrelated b-min-sep paper 2602.09338. Documentation half verified: docs/reference/accounting.md:238-259, docs/user-guide/accounting.md:122-140 and docs/mechanisms/index.md:88 document the truncated form only as 'weaker than plain Poisson', with no statement that the guarantee is conditioned on a fixed, public |D| (p_trunc = Pr[Binom(n-1,q) >= B] at truncated_poisson.rs:96-103 makes the analysis n-specific) and no mention of the source's caution about composing it; the documented composed example reproduces (Accountant() | poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01, truncated_batch_size=600, dataset_size=50000) | gaussian(2.0) -> epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.9944, no warning). Two corrections. First, affects_epsilon is false: nothing here shows a number that is too small — the implementation's second mixture component is a Replace-adjacency PLD at sigma/2 (doubled sensitivity), truncated epsilon measured >= plain Poisson at the same rate (0.19952 vs 0.19945), and the reporter's own numerical work found it dominating the paper's pair by 1-19x. Second, 'silently switches the adjacency relation' overstates: the code analyses the ordinary add/remove pair (D of size n, D minus one record) that Opaque documents; what is undocumented is that the pair must be at the specific n passed in, i.e. |D| is treated as public and fixed. Net: a citation-integrity plus doc-caveat defect, low severity — and a live one, since #418 'Audit and repair scholarly references' is closed.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader of truncated_poisson.rs (or a reviewer following the repo's own DP-review protocol) hits '[Gan25]' twice, finds no definition anywhere in the repository and no arXiv identifier, and cannot reach the source (Ganesh, 'Tighter Privacy Analysis for Truncated Poisson Sampling', arXiv:2508.15089) to check the mixture formula or its hypotheses. Separately, a user following docs/reference/accounting.md:250-259 composes the truncated step with other releases and gets epsilon = 1.9944 with no indication that the analysis is conditioned on the specific dataset size passed in (|D| public and fixed) or that the source recommends care when composing that result. No evidence was found that the reported epsilon is anti-conservative — the shipped mixture is at least as large as plain Poisson at the same rate.

verdicts.title: lambda-CGD sensitivity is documented as "Theorem 1, eq 15 of the paper" — Theorem 1's hypotheses do not cover the default normalized mechanism, and eq (15) is a utility metric, not a sensitivity
verdicts.reasoning: Verified against the primary source itself (fetched arXiv:2601.22334 PDF and extracted the text). Theorem 1 reads verbatim 'Theorem 1 (Theorem 2 from Kalinin and Lampert [2024]). Let C be a lower triangular Toeplitz matrix with decreasing non-negative entries c_0 >= ... >= c_{n-1} >= 0. Then, under b-min-separation, the sensitivity is given by sens_{k,b}(C) = ||sum_{j=0}^{k-1} C[:,jb+1]||_2, (3)' — generic, no closed form in lambda. Equation (14), inside the proof of Lemma 2, is the closed-form squared sensitivity of the unnormalized C_lambda ('= (1-lambda^{2b}) / ((1-lambda^2)(1-lambda^b)^2) sum_{j=1}^{k} (1-lambda^{bj})^2'), which is exactly the formula the repo ships; equation (15) is 'The squared maximum row l2-norm of the matrix A C_lambda^{-1} is ||A C_lambda^{-1}||^2_{2->infty} = 1 + (1-lambda)^2 (n-1)', a MaxSE utility quantity. The paper also states 'The matrix C_lambda D^{-1} is no longer Toeplitz, and therefore the sensitivity Theorem 1 cannot be applied directly. In this work, we generalize the sensitivity theorem specifically for the normalized DP-lambda-CGD ... Lemma 8 ... (12)'. So docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:70-73 mis-cites on both counts, and the default path is normalized=True (_lambda_cgd.py:171-181 routes to lambda_cgd_normalized_sensitivity_squared). The same mis-citation appears in the Rust header and function docs (matrix_factorization/lambda_cgd.rs:8, :65, :130) where the displayed formula is in fact eq (14); the normalized function there does cite Lemma 8 correctly (:161). Low severity, no epsilon impact: the numbers are not in question (the module's own tests and the reporter's brute-force check agree), only the pointer a reviewer would follow. Live gap — the citation-repair issue #418 is closed.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reviewer following docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:70-73 (and the matching Rust header at matrix_factorization/lambda_cgd.rs:8/:65) to arXiv:2601.22334 finds that Theorem 1 is the generic Toeplitz min-sep formula with no lambda closed form, that eq (15) is the row-norm ||A C_lambda^{-1}||^2_{2->infty} used for MaxSE rather than any sensitivity, and that the paper explicitly says Theorem 1 does not apply to the column-normalized matrix that lambda_cgd_strategy uses by default. The correct pointers — eq (14) for normalized=False and Lemma 8 / eq (12) for the normalized default — are never given in the docs, so the reviewer cannot confirm what lambda_cgd_normalized_sensitivity_squared computes. Implementation correctness is unaffected.

verdicts.title: Balls-in-Bins modules cite "Definition 3.1" and "Lemma 3.2" of a paper whose arXiv id they never give, next to a URL for a different paper that contains neither result
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified. Repo side: opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:3-5 and :10 attribute Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.2 to 'Choquette-Choo et al. 2024' while its References block (:23-27) lists only https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16802 (Chua et al.) plus an unlinked, truncated 'Choquette-Choo et al. (2024), "Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms"'; the accountant module _balls_in_bins.py:11 and :31-36 repeats the pattern with the full title but again no URL. Only the Rust monte_carlo.rs:3-4, :28-29 gives title plus https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06266. Paper side: I extracted every numbered result from the 2412.16802 PDF — Definition 2.1, 2.2, Lemma 2.3, Propositions 2.4/2.5/2.6/3.2/3.3, Theorems 2.5/3.1/3.3/3.4/4.1/4.2 — there is no Definition 3.1 and no Lemma 3.2 in that paper. In arXiv:2410.06266 both exist and match the code: Definition 3.1 is balls-in-bins batching (each example independently into exactly one of b batches, round-robin), and Lemma 3.2 (Dimension-reduction for balls-in-bins batching) states 'Suppose C in R^{n x n} is a lower-triangular matrix with non-negative entries. Then P, Q (resp. Q, P) as defined above is a dominating pair ... under the add (resp. remove) adjacency', with P = (1/b) sum N(m_i, sigma^2 I), m_i = sum_{j=0}^{E-1} |C|[:, b*j+i] — exactly the construction the accountant docstring writes down. One sub-claim refuted: 'Chua et al. (2025)' is a legitimate venue-year citation (the paper appeared at AISTATS 2025), so the date is not an error. Citation hygiene only, no epsilon or behavioral impact; live because #418 'Audit and repair scholarly references' is closed.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reviewer checking that the shipped BnB dominating pair matches its source opens the only URL either Python module offers (arXiv:2412.16802, Chua et al.) and finds no Definition 3.1 and no Lemma 3.2 — that paper's numbered results are Definitions 2.1-2.2, Lemma 2.3, Propositions 2.4-2.6/3.2-3.3 and Theorems 2.5/3.1/3.3/3.4/4.1/4.2. The results actually being relied on, including the hypothesis that C be lower-triangular with non-negative entries (which every correlated strategy the module accepts must satisfy), are in arXiv:2410.06266, cited in both Python modules without a URL and, in the sampler, under a truncated title. No numerical claim is wrong; the reader simply cannot reach the source from the module.
